title: How a Prince Learned to Read
author: James Baldwin
summary: 阿尔弗雷德王子为了读懂一本书而学识字，胜过兄弟们的弓、鹰与偏见。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1912 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: A thousand years ago boys and girls did not learn to read. Books were very scarce and very precious, and only a few men could read them.
paragraphs.zh: 一千年前，男孩女孩都不上学读书。书籍非常稀少、非常珍贵，只有少数人识字。

paragraphs.en: Each book was written with a pen or a brush. The pictures were painted by hand, and some of them were very beautiful. A good book would sometimes cost as much as a good house.
paragraphs.zh: 每本书都是用笔或刷子写成的。书中的图画是手工绘制的，有些非常精美。一本好书有时贵得像一栋好房子。

paragraphs.en: In those times there were even some kings who could not read. They thought more of hunting and fighting than of learning.
paragraphs.zh: 在那个时代，甚至有些国王也不识字。他们更看重打猎和打仗，而不是读书学习。

paragraphs.en: There was one such king who had four sons, Ethelbald, Ethelbert, Ethelred, and Alfred. The three older boys were sturdy, half-grown lads; the youngest, Alfred, was a slender, fair-haired child.
paragraphs.zh: 就有这样一位国王，他有四个儿子：埃塞尔博尔德、埃塞尔伯特、埃塞尔雷德和阿尔弗雷德。三个年长的男孩都是结实、半大的小伙子；最小的阿尔弗雷德却是个纤细、金发的孩子。

paragraphs.en: One day when they were with their mother, she showed them a wonderful book that some rich friend had given her. She turned the leaves and showed them the strange letters. She showed them the beautiful pictures, and told them how they had been drawn and painted.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，孩子们和母亲在一起，母亲拿出一本一位富有的朋友送给她的奇妙的书。她翻动书页，指给他们看那些陌生的字母，给他们看美丽的图画，还告诉他们这些画是怎样画出来的。

paragraphs.en: They admired the book very much, for they had never seen anything like it. "But the best part of it is the story which it tells," said their mother. "If you could only read, you might learn that story and enjoy it. Now I have a mind to give this book to one of you"
paragraphs.zh: 他们非常喜爱这本书，因为他们从未见过这样的东西。“但这本书最好的部分是它讲的故事，”母亲说，“如果你们能读书，就能知道那个故事，享受其中的乐趣。现在我打算把这本书送给你们中的一个。”

paragraphs.en: "Will you give it to me, mother?" asked little Alfred.
paragraphs.zh: “母亲，您会把它给我吗？”小阿尔弗雷德问。

paragraphs.en: "I will give it to the one who first learns to read in it" she answered.
paragraphs.zh: “谁先学会读这本书，我就把它给谁。”母亲回答。

paragraphs.en: "I am sure I would rather have a good bow with arrows" said Ethelred.
paragraphs.zh: “我肯定更想要一把好弓和几支箭。”埃塞尔雷德说。

paragraphs.en: "And I would rather have a young hawk that has been trained to hunt" said Ethelbert.
paragraphs.zh: “我更想要一只训练过打猎的小鹰。”埃塞尔伯特说。

paragraphs.en: "If I were a priest or a monk" said Ethelbald, "I would learn to read. But I am a prince, and it is foolish for princes to waste their time with such things."
paragraphs.zh: “如果我是神父或修士，”埃塞尔博尔德说，“我就会学识字。可我是王子，王子把时间浪费在这种事上太愚蠢了。”

paragraphs.en: "But I should like to know the story which this book tells," said Alfred.
paragraphs.zh: “可我想知道这本书讲的故事。”阿尔弗雷德说。
